chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hasan al-Taymi, from Muhammad ibn Tasneem the scribe, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Amr, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Amr al-Azraq, who said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying, and a man asked him about a man who died and left a daughter of his sister, and left mawali (freed slaves), and for him, with me, are a thousand dirhams, and no one knew about it. So the daughter of his sister came and pledged a mus'haf (Quran codex) with me as security, so I gave her thirty dirhams. So Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to me: 'When I told him, did anyone know about it?' I said, 'No.' He said: 'So give it to her piece by piece, and do not let anyone know.'

key_terms.ابْنَةُ أُخْتٍ: Daughter of the sister (paternal aunt's daughter)

ai.seo_question: How should hidden cash from an estate be distributed to an heir if no one else knows about it?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* illustrates the principle of *sitr* (discretion) in inheritance distribution, where Imam al-Sadiq (AS) advises giving the hidden wealth to the sister's daughter in installments to prevent others from discovering and claiming it. It highlights the flexibility of Shia jurisprudence in handling *mawali* (freed slaves) and distant relatives when explicit heirs are absent, emphasizing practical wisdom over rigid procedural disclosure. The ruling underscores the Imam's authority to determine equitable distribution based on the specific circumstances of the estate and the claimant's status.
